title: Widget cost budgets and aggregation guidance for inference dashboards
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures pragmatic guidance for building inference-focused dashboards that balance signal quality with backend query cost. The goal is to reduce surprise billing from exploratory widgets, keep panel compute under control for large time ranges, and ensure teams have consistent, actionable aggregates for incident response and regressions.

Scope:
- Applies to dashboards that surface model inference telemetry (latency, token throughput, KV cache hit, batch size distributions, fallback rates, model variant routing).
- Covers metric types (gauge, counter/histogram), aggregation windows, sampling strategies, trace-tagging conventions, and dashboard-level cost budgets.
- Does NOT replace SLI/SLO definitions; it complements them by focusing on observability cost and dashboard ergonomics.

Principles (short):
1) Default to coarse aggregates for long time ranges (>=7d) and finer granularity for 1h-24h ranges.
2) Prefer pre-aggregated rollups or downsampled materialized views for heavy-hit widgets.
3) Limit cardinality in dashboard queries: prefer service/model tier/value buckets over free-form tags.
4) Use sampling and traces sparingly in summary widgets; surface traces only in drilldowns.
5) Assign a cost budget to each dashboard and a primary owner for cost exceptions.

Metric naming and types (recommendation):
- Namespace: inference.<component>.<metric> (e.g., inference.serving.latency_ms_p95)
- Suffixes: _count for counters, _ms for latencies, _ratio for ratios, _hits/_misses for cache stats, _samples for sampled counts.
- Histogram vs summary: Prefer histograms exported as pre-bucketed where possible to allow rollups; avoid unbounded summary metrics for long-range queries.

Aggregation windows and retention guidance:
- 1m resolution: default for 0-24h panels (good for realtime ops).
- 5m resolution: default for 1d-7d panels (reduce cost).
- 1h resolution: default for >7d retrospectives and weekly/monthly reports.
- Materialize commonly-used aggregates (token-rate per model, avg latency by variant) into a daily/hourly rollup table to avoid repeated heavy queries.

Example Prometheus-style guidance (conceptual; our exporters map to Prom/TS DB semantics):
- Avoid `rate()` over high-cardinality labels without grouping. Instead do:
  sum by(model, region) (rate(inference_request_total{env="prod"}[5m]))
- For percentiles, compute at ingestion or use histogram_quantile on pre-bucketed histogram metric:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, model) (inference_latency_ms_bucket{env="prod"}))
- For long-range trend charts use precomputed series: inference_token_rate_hourly

Example BigQuery/ClickHouse guidance for analytics-backed panels:
- Use partitioned tables by day and pre-aggregate hourly/day buckets for heavy panels.
- Sample SQL for a 7d 5m-bucketed token-rate (simplified):
  SELECT
    TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_time, MINUTE, 5) as window_start,
    model_name,
    SUM(tokens_generated) / 300 AS tokens_per_sec
  FROM inference.events_prod
  WHERE event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY window_start, model_name
  ORDER BY window_start ASC;
- If querying user-provided prompts, ensure PII is filtered at ingestion; avoid full-text scans in dashboards.

Cardinality controls and recommended label sets:
- Allowed high-cardinality labels: request_id, trace_id (never used for rollups or group_by).
- Use these labels for drilldowns only (hidden panel filters).
- Recommended grouping keys for most panels: {service, model_name, model_variant, region, capacity_tier}. Keep additional labels to a max of 3 in group_by.

Sampling and traces:
- Traces: default sample rate of 1% globally for production inference traffic. Increase to 10% for canary or traffic-sampled subsets only.
- For latency reduction debugging, use an adaptive sampler that keeps more traces when latency SLI breaches a threshold (e.g., 3x baseline).
- Add tags on spans: model_name, model_variant, host_pool, batch_size. Avoid including prompt text or user identifiers.

Dashboard-level cost budgets and guardrails:
- Assign an estimated monthly query cost (low/medium/high) to each dashboard. Default medium = 0.5% of observability budget.
- Enforce query timeouts at the visual platform: 30s for interactive panels, 120s for scheduled exports.
- Block dashboards with open free-text filters that expand cardinality above 100k unique values.
- Require an owner and cost justification for dashboards tagged high-cost.

Widget patterns (recommended):
- Overview bar (cheap): single-number KPIs (p95 latency, token/sec, errors/sec) using pre-aggregates.
- Trend canvas: 1-3 lines per chart, grouped by model tier not by unique model by default. Use 5m or 1h rollups depending on range.
- Heatmap for latency slices: use BQ materialized hourly histogram rather than raw per-request histogram queries.
- Drilldown row: collapsible panels that run heavier queries only on expansion; default collapsed.
- Trace launcher: a button on panel to fetch recent traces for the selected timeslice (traces fetched asynchronously to avoid blocking).

Ownership and lifecycle:
- Dashboard owner must review panels monthly; mark panels with a last-reviewed timestamp.
- Decommission policy: dashboards with no edits and <5 views/month for 90 days -> archive.
- Cost exceptions: owner opens Obs-Cost ticket (JIRA-OBS-COST) to request increased budget; must include query plan and expected query volume.

Operational playbook snippets:
- Incident triage: use low-cost overview + 1 pre-approved drilldown. If triage requires ad-hoc queries that exceed budget, open a short-lived query slot and have SRE review results.
- Regression investigation: compare pre-rollout and post-rollout hourly rollups; avoid ad-hoc full retention scans until a hypothesis is formed.

Implementation checklist (minimal):
- [ ] Identify top 10 heavy widgets across prod dashboards (owner: analytics team)
- [ ] Create hourly rollups for those signals (owner: infra/ingest)
- [ ] Add dashboard metadata: owner, estimated-monthly-cost, last-reviewed (owner: dashboard creator)
- [ ] Set dashboard default time-range to 7d and use 5m rollups by default (owner: observability UX)
- [ ] Add adaptive trace sampler for latency SLI breach (owner: tracing team)

Open questions / things to decide:
- How fine-grained should auto-rollups be by model_variant vs model_name? (cost vs signal tradeoff)
- What is our cross-team quota enforcement mechanism for dashboard compute? (central billing tag or enforced by platform?)
- Should we provide a gallery of cost-optimized sample widgets for engineers to copy?

Appendix: example metric-to-rollup mapping (proposal)
- inference_request_total -> hourly request_count rollup (by model, variant, region)
- inference_latency_ms_bucket -> hourly histogram rollup (same dims)
- tokens_generated -> hourly token_count (for cost estimation and billing)

Short glossary:
- Rollup: pre-aggregated view stored at fixed intervals to speed long-range queries.
- Cardinality: number of distinct values on a label; high cardinality increases query cost.
- Bucketed histogram: latency distribution split into fixed buckets at ingestion time.

If you own or frequently edit inference-related dashboards, please review this doc and add a short note with your blockers. Plan: iterate with analytics and tracing teams during Feb 2026 sprint to land the top 10 rollups.
